title: Make editor preview ownership structural (marker, not scene names/prefixes)
description:
## Summary

Replace name/prefix-based rediscovery and destruction of the editor preview with explicit structural ownership. An external audit (P2) found the extracted `CreaturePreviewController` still locates "its" root via `GameObject.Find("CreatureCreator Preview")` and destroys children whose names begin with a fixed prefix, an implicit ownership protocol that can adopt or destroy unrelated objects.

Provenance: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-deep-dive-code-review-audit-26-09-05-23-07-45.md` F4 (P2). Verified at current HEAD `99fe6ad`. Broad owner family: TSK-0098 (editor decomposition) / TSK-0104 (generated Unity-object ownership). No existing TSK owns the marker-based ownership fix explicitly.

## Scope

`Assets/Scripts/Editor/CreaturePreviewController.cs` (and its callers in `CreatureEditorWindow` / request-state):

- Give the preview root an explicit ownership marker (a small editor marker component or an explicit instance-registered handle), not a human-readable scene name.
- Recover the preview root by that marker across domain reload, not by `GameObject.Find(PreviewObjectName)`.
- Destroy only objects this controller explicitly created/registered; do not infer child ownership from the `"CreatureCreator Preview Geometry "` name prefix.
- Separate display name from identity; stop coupling the object name to ownership.
- Avoid a generic repository/DI container; a marker + clear owned-lifecycle list is sufficient.
- Preserve existing preview regeneration, stale blocking, and disposal behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused editor test proves an unrelated GameObject with the same root name (`"CreatureCreator Preview"`) and a child with the same geometry prefix is never adopted, modified, or destroyed by the controller.
- The preview root is re-found after a simulated domain reload by marker, not by name.
- Only controller-owned children are cleaned up on regeneration/dispose.
- Existing preview tests remain green.

## Validation

Focused EditMode tests under `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Editor/` for the ownership marker and the unrelated same-name/same-prefix case, plus a manual SceneView check that preview regeneration and cleanup behave as before. Static source inspection alone cannot close this task.

## Findings

- The controller does not own a durable root reference across all create/reload paths; it re-discovers "its" object from a global scene namespace and infers child ownership from names.
- An unrelated same-name root can be adopted and an unrelated prefixed child can be destroyed.
- The recent extraction moved the brittle protocol into a smaller class rather than replacing it.

## Blockers

None known.

## Next Step

Add the marker/owned-lifecycle mechanism and the unrelated-object regression test.

comments.body:
Round 3 implementation + validation evidence.

Changed files:
- Assets/Scripts/Editor/CreaturePreviewController.cs — replaced GameObject.Find("CreatureCreator Preview") + name-prefix child destruction with structural ownership: root and each geometry child are registered by EntityId handle persisted in SessionState (RootEntityKey/GeometryEntityIdsKey, ulong strings). RecoverExistingPreview()/EnsurePreviewRoot() recover via EditorUtility.EntityIdToObject; ClearGeometryObjects() destroys only registered entity handles. Root display name kept display-only; identity is the handle. Regeneration order (ApplyPreviewMesh->ClearGeometryObjects), stale blocking, and Dispose semantics unchanged.
- Assets/Scripts/Editor/CreatureEditorWindow.cs — OnEnable now constructs the controller then sets _previewGameObject = _previewController.RecoverExistingPreview() (no name-based GameObject.Find).
- Assets/Scripts/Tests/Editor/CreaturePreviewControllerOwnershipTests.cs — new EditMode fixture (4 tests): unrelated same-name root + old-prefix child never adopted/modified/destroyed; root re-found by handle across simulated reload; unregistered same-name root ignored; regeneration destroys only registered geometry children.

Validation:
- dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Editor.csproj --no-restore: Build succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor.csproj --no-restore: Build succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- git diff --check: exit 0.
- Unity EditMode (connected, port 6401): focused CreaturePreviewControllerOwnershipTests 4/4 passed; full ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor assembly 129/129 passed.

Design note / non-obvious decision: Unity 6000 cannot attach Editor-assembly MonoBehaviours to scene objects ("Can't add script behaviour ... editor script"), so a component marker is not viable. Used the task's alternative "explicit instance-registered handle": Unity 6000 EntityId persisted in SessionState (EntityId.FromULong/ToULong static; GetEntityId/EntityIdToObject; GetInstanceID/InstanceIDToObject are obsolete-as-error in this version). No generic repository/DI added; no runtime coupling; no competing ownership scheme. Not committed; orchestrator to commit/push after review. Status left for orchestrator.

comments.body: Orchestrator Round 3 review (2026-09-05/06 deep-dive hardening sprint): diff independently reviewed. Scope clean (CreaturePreviewController.cs ownership model, CreatureEditorWindow.cs OnEnable recovery line only, new ownership test fixture + meta, task record). Verified the source replaces GameObject.Find + name-prefix destruction with SessionState-persisted Unity 6000 EntityId handles; RecoverExistingPreview/EnsurePreviewRoot recover by handle, ClearGeometryObjects destroys only registered handles, display name decoupled from identity, regeneration order + stale-blocking + Dispose preserved. Acceptance tests are meaningful: unrelated same-name root + old-prefix child never adopted/modified/destroyed; recovery by handle across simulated reload; unregistered same-name root ignored; regeneration destroys only registered children. Evidence confidence: source + tests spot-checked by orchestrator (read full diffs/test); Unity EditMode focused 4/4 + full editor 129/129 and both dotnet builds are report-trusted from the subagent. git diff --check clean. Residual risk: hard (real) domain reload not forced (simulated only) — relies on Unity 6000 EntityId stability for the editor-created root; if a real reload fails to recover, RecoverExistingPreview returns null and regeneration recreates the root (behavior preserved). Marking Done.
